job.style: a passage rich in numbers, dates or measurements

response.passage: In the bustling town of Kolar, young inventor Arjun decided to test the magnetic effects of electric current on June 12th. He used a copper wire coiled 45 times around an iron nail to create an electromagnet. Arjun observed that when he connected the wire to a 9-volt battery, the nail attracted small iron filings. His friend, Meera, watched closely as Arjun increased the current flow, which caused the magnetic field to strengthen significantly. Arjun noted that the strength of the magnet depends on the number of turns in the coil. He also tested a silver ring, but it remained unaffected by the current. By July 15th, Arjun had documented that the magnetic field disappears immediately when the circuit is broken. He concluded that the flow of electricity is the primary cause of the magnetism in his device. Unlike a permanent magnet, this device requires a constant power source to function. Arjun hopes to present his findings at the Kolar Science Fair next year to show how electricity can be harnessed for practical work.
response.summary: Arjun built an electromagnet using a battery and a coiled wire in Kolar. He discovered that the magnetic field strength increases with more current and disappears when the circuit is broken.
